explanation: The theorem says that a matrix in GL₂(K_w) lies in the range of GL.map (algebraMap O K_w) exactly when both x and x⁻¹ have all entries in O. Here Kw is the library's own `LocalGL2.integralSubgroup`, which is defined as `(Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map (algebraMap R K)).range`. I grepped Mathlib for `GeneralLinearGroup.map` and for range or membership lemmas about GL, Units.map and matrix entries. The only hits were `Projective.lean`, `Basic.lean` and `CongruenceSubgroups.lean`, and none states an entries-integral characterisation of the range of GL.map. I found no general lemma saying that a unit matrix over K with integral entries and integral inverse entries comes from GL over the subring.
